fact: 1921年美国处于1920—1921年严重衰退的谷底。批发价格从1920年到1921年下跌超过36%（一说超过30%），是美国历史上最严重的通缩之一。失业率从1920年的5.2%升至1921年峰值11.7%。生铁产量从1920年10月的329.3万吨降至1921年1月的240.2万吨——为1915年5月以来最低（排除1919年罢工月份）。1921年全年钢锭产量仅1950万吨（第一季度年化2500万吨→第三季度1450万吨）。

sources.title: The Commercial Financial Chronicle, Vol. 112, Feb. 5, 1921（圣路易斯联储FRASER存档）
sources.quote: Iron production in the United States in January 1921 aggregated only 2,401,845 tons, against 2,703,855 tons in December 1920... not since May 1915, apart from May, June and October (strike months) 1919, has so little pig iron been made in any month as in January.

fact: 1921年4月12日，美国钢铁公司（U.S. Steel）宣布将基础售价平均下调约7美元/吨（以匹兹堡离岸价为基准），4月13日生效。钢坯从38.50美元/吨降至37美元，板材从42美元降至39美元，线材从52美元降至48美元，锡板从7美元/基箱降至6.25美元。4月8日Republic Iron & Steel率先提价2美元/吨后，独立厂商纷纷跟进，但钢铁公司随即大幅降价。5月3日钢铁公司宣布日工工资下调约20%，5月16日生效。

sources.title: The Commercial Financial Chronicle, May 7, 1921（圣路易斯联储FRASER存档）
sources.quote: On April 12 came the announcement of the action of the Steel Corporation. A reduction of an average of about $7 per ton from the 1919 prices was announced in a schedule of nine items. Steel billets were marked down from $38.50 to $37 per gross ton... 'we have decided to substantially reduce the base selling prices of our commodities, f.o.b. Pittsburgh, to take effect April 13 1921'... On May 3 a statement was issued, saying: 'The wage rates of day labor at the manufacturing plants of the Steel Corporation have been decreased about 20%, to become effective May 16.'

fact: 1921年1月28日，福特汽车公司高地公园工厂（Highland Park plant）部分复工，产能仅为25%—30%。该厂于1920年12月23日关闭时正常雇员约5万人。复工后计划日产1500—2000辆（关闭前日产约4000辆），工资最低标准维持每日6美元。1920年5月至1921年7月，全美汽车产量下降约60%。

sources.title: The Commercial Financial Chronicle, Feb. 5, 1921（圣路易斯联储FRASER存档）
sources.quote: in Detroit, the Highland Park plant of the Ford Motor Company resumed operations in part at the close of the month—that is, on Monday, January 28. The plant, however, is at the outset to be operated at only about 25% to 30% of its capacity. This plant was closed down on December 23, at which time the normal complement of its force was about 50,000. ... the rates of wage will be the same as before, that is, on a minimum basis of $6 per day... The company plans to begin the production of from 1,500 to 2,000 cars a day. The average before the plant closed down was around 4,000 a day.

fact: 1921年美国钢铁业工资大幅下调：Bethlehem Steel约90%的员工面临10%—20%的工资削减；Colorado Fuel & Iron全厂减薪15%；美国钢铁公司薄板厂减薪10%（2月1日生效），后全厂日工减薪约20%（5月16日生效）。钢铁工人从正常的8000—10000人减至不到3000人（Bethlehem Steelton厂）。批发价格下降超过36%使生活成本降低，但大规模失业抵消了这一好处。

sources.title: The Commercial Financial Chronicle, Feb. 5, 1921
sources.quote: instances of reductions in wages ranging from 10% to 25% were quite numerous. Conspicuous among the companies making reductions in wages was the Bethlehem Steel Corporation... fully 90% of the company's men would be subject to wage cuts varying from 10% to 20%. ... Colorado Fuel & Iron Company agreed to a 15% reduction in wages in all departments.

fact: 1920—1921年美国联邦储备在纽约联储行长本杰明·斯特朗主导下急剧加息以抑制通胀和稳定货币。财政部长梅隆推动减税（削减超额利润税和高所得税率）以刺激投资。政府避免直接救济和大规模公共工程。1921年下半年经济开始V型复苏，1922年工业生产强劲反弹。纽约证券交易所随后进入「咆哮的二十年代」历史牛市。

sources.title: LLMpedia, Recession of 1920–1921
sources.quote: the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, under Benjamin Strong Jr., sharply raised interest rates in late 1919 and 1920 to curb speculation and stabilize the currency. ... Secretary of the Treasury Andrew W. Mellon advocated for and implemented significant tax cuts, including reductions to the excess profits tax and high-income rates, to stimulate investment. ... Recovery began in the second half of 1921 and proved remarkably swift. ... The New York Stock Exchange embarked on a historic bull market.

fact: 1921年美国钢铁和汽车业处于衰退谷底，但为随后的技术升级奠定基础。钢铁价格已从1919年高位大幅回落（钢坯从38.50美元/吨降至37美元，薄板从3.55美元/百磅降至3.10美元）。1922年1月的行业展望认为汽车、石油和罐头业将是新需求来源：1922年汽车用钢预计约70万长吨，锡板预计约150万长吨，石油业每年消耗超100万长吨管材。

sources.title: The New York Times, Outlook for Steel Good in Some Lines（1922-01-16）
sources.quote: Production of steel ingots in December was at the rate of 20,000,000 tons a year... Production in the year as a whole was 19,500,000 tons. ... The automobile industry has liquidated its stocks of steel and is ordering somewhat more freely. The amount of steel used in making passenger automobiles in 1922... will be about 700,000 gross tons. ... The oil industry... has lately been taking more than a million gross tons a year of tubular goods.

fact: 1921年匹兹堡钢铁业严重失业：Bethlehem Steelton厂从正常的8000—10000人减至不到3000人；大量工人被解雇或减薪。1921年匹兹堡和底特律是「工业城市失业特别严重」的代表。但也正是在这一萧条谷底，设备、专利和工厂以极低价格出售，为随后的「咆哮的二十年代」提供了廉价收购窗口。

sources.title: The Commercial Financial Chronicle, Feb. 5, 1921
sources.quote: three large departments of the Steelton plant of the Bethlehem Steel Company had closed for an indefinite period and that this reduced the number of men employed to less than 3,000 as against 8,000 to 10,000, the number in normal times.
